title: Snow & Winter Play
strapline: The garden has vanished under a soft white blanket overnight — hats on, gloves on, out before it goes.
intent: Snow transforms the whole familiar outdoor world overnight, and provision that seizes the rare snowy morning gives children an experience of wonder they will remember for years.
Rolling, digging, patting and building in snow is powerful whole-body work — heaving, lifting, balancing on slippery ground.
Snow is a wide-open investigation: children discover it is cold, it melts in warm hands, it squashes and packs, and it turns to water indoors.
The changed landscape and the melting that follows connect children to the coldest season and to change of state, all felt first-hand.
Making footprints, tracks and patterns in fresh snow is mark-making and early recording on the biggest, most exciting canvas of the year.
Wintry language falls like the snow — snowflake, freezing, melt, footprint, snowball, slippery, sparkle.
implementation: The moment snow falls, get everyone kitted out — warm layers, waterproofs, gloves — and out into it while it is fresh and deep.
Let children lead: rolling snowballs, building, digging, stamping tracks, catching flakes, watching snow melt in a warm glove.
Wonder alongside them: 'Where do you think the snow will be first to disappear? What happens if we bring a handful inside?'
Bring a tray of snow in to investigate warm — watch it turn to water, add colour, mould it — and compare with the icy garden outside.
Weave in maths and comparison — whose snowball is biggest, count the footprints, sort the deep snow from the trodden-flat snow.
Record the disappearing act: photograph the white garden in the morning and the wet grass by home time, and talk about where it all went.
key_questions: Where do you think the snow will disappear first?
What happens if we bring a handful inside?
How many footprints can you count in the fresh snow?
Where did all the snow go by home time?

impact.text: Children discover that snow is cold, melts in warm hands, packs and turns to water indoors.
Children roll, dig, pat and build — powerful whole-body work on slippery ground.
Children connect the changed landscape and the melting to the coldest season and change of state.
Children make footprints, tracks and patterns — mark-making on the biggest canvas of the year.
Children gain wintry words — snowflake, freezing, melt, footprint, snowball, slippery, sparkle.

enhancements: Warm layers, waterproofs and gloves so children get straight out into fresh snow.
A tray of snow brought in to watch turn to water and mould warm.
Before-and-after photos of the white garden and the wet grass by home time.
Colour added to snow for mark-making and pattern.

playing_exploring: Children explore snow with their whole bodies, rolling, building, digging and stamping in a rare, transformed world.
They test what snow does — how it packs, how it melts, how cold it really is.
active_learning: Children work hard and persist at building and shaping in the snow, undaunted by cold hands and slippery ground.
creating_thinking: Children predict where snow will melt first and what happens when it comes indoors, linking the cold and the warmth to what they see.
